{{Short description|French planetary scientist}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=March 2023}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=March 2023}}
'''Dominique Bockelée-Morvan''' (born 1957) is a French [[astrophysics|astrophysicist]] and [[planetary science|planetary scientist]] specializing in the molecular composition of [[comet]]s.{{r|schmadel}}  She is a director of research for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS), affiliated with the [[Paris Observatory]],{{r|cnrs}} and a former president of Commission 15 on the Physical Study of Comets & Minor Planets of the [[International Astronomical Union]].{{r|iau}}

==Education and career==
Bockelée-Morvan earned a doctorate in 1987 through [[Paris Diderot University]], with the dissertation ''Les conditions d'excitation des molecules meres dans les atmospheres cometaires : applications a l'eau et a l'acide cyanhydrique'', supervised by Jacques Crovisier.{{r|these}}

She was president of Commission 15 on the Physical Study of Comets & Minor Planets of the [[International Astronomical Union]], from 2012 to 2015.{{r|iau}}

==Research==
Bockelée-Morvan brought the study of comets from a (literally) dusty backwater of planetary science into the mainstream.{{r|cnrs|argent}}
Through infrared and radio observations of comets,{{r|cnrs}} and the development of excitation models for cometary chemicals,{{r|schmadel}} she has found over 20 different molecular impurities in their ice.{{r|cnrs}} Her work found connections between the makeup of comets and of the [[interstellar medium]], and with [[Prebiotic (chemistry)|prebiotic chemistry]].{{r|argent}} She has also helped explain the 3.4&nbsp;μm-wavelength emissions of comets.{{r|schmadel}}

She has been a collaborator on the MIRO and VIRTIS experiments on the [[Rosetta (spacecraft)|Rosetta space probe]] and its 2014 flyby study of comet [[67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko]].{{r|cnrs|argent}} Beyond comets, she has also contributed to the first discovery of [[water vapor]] on the asteroid [[Ceres (dwarf planet)|Ceres]].{{r|argent}}

==Recognition==
Bockelée-Morvan was the 1991 winner of the {{ill|Thorlet Prize|fr|Prix Thorlet}} of the [[French Academy of Sciences]], for her studies of [[Halley's Comet]]. She won the young researcher prize of the [[Société Française d'Astronomie et d'Astrophysique]] (SF2A) in 1992.{{r|obsprix}}

She received the David Bates Medal of the [[European Geosciences Union]] in 2002, "for her exceptional observations and interpretations of the composition of comets".{{r|bates}} She received the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2014.{{r|cnrs|argent}}

Asteroid [[4020 Dominique]], discovered in 1981, was named after Bockelée-Morvan.{{r|schmadel}}
